claims_reproduced: Matrix-free Arnoldi/Krylov exp(tA)v implementation is numerically correct (Arnoldi relation and orthonormal V at ~1e-15)
Exponential propagation accuracy improves strongly with Krylov dimension K and supports the paper’s practical sweet-spot around K≈20 for ~1e-4 tolerances
Exponential propagation is unconditionally stable in the Stokes/linear-diffusion limit with very large effective timesteps (monotone decay, no blow-up)
Inexact Newton with fixed-K GMRES exhibits linear (not quadratic) convergence behavior consistent with fixed relative linear-solve accuracy controlling progress
Diminishing returns beyond K≈30 for Newton-Krylov inner iterations (little improvement in final nonlinear residual beyond K~30)
IRAM/implicitly restarted Arnoldi (via ARPACK) recovers leading eigenvalues accurately and shows no benefit from increasing total subspace beyond ~30 in this setting
Storage scaling dominated by N×K Krylov basis V rather than dense N×N storage
claims_not_reproduced: Couette–Taylor (Chebyshev–Fourier pseudospectral, cylindrical geometry) bifurcation to wavy vortices at the paper’s parameters
Paper’s specific steady-state and stability results for Couette–Taylor (e.g., Fig. 8/9/10 tied to that discretization and pressure/Poisson coupling)
Performance/timing comparisons against 1990s semi-implicit methods on Cray-class hardware
one_line: Rebuilt and exercised the three Krylov methodologies on faithful PDE analogs, confirming key K-sweet-spot and stability/convergence behaviors, but not the Couette–Taylor application results.
justification: The replication independently implements and tests the paper’s three core methodological components (Krylov exponential propagation, Newton–Krylov steady solving, and IRAM eigenanalysis) on nontrivial PDE discretizations, with quantitative checks against dense ground truth where feasible. It verifies the main behavioral claims about accuracy/stability and the practical Krylov-dimension sweet spot (K≈20–30), and reproduces the diminishing-returns regime for larger K. However, it does not reproduce the paper’s flagship Couette–Taylor pseudospectral experiments or the associated wavy-vortex eigenvalue results, which are central application demonstrations even if the original code was unavailable. Overall, the methodological conclusions are strongly supported, but coverage is incomplete because the domain-specific Couette–Taylor validation is not rerun.
